gloss: to strip, to peel off, to tear off

definitions.gloss: to strip off, to peel off, to tear off
definitions.explanation: To forcefully remove something that covers or clings to a surface — such as skin, bark, clothing, paint, or a mask. Implies a rougher, more forceful action than simply peeling.

examples.japanese: {皮|かわ}を{剥|は}いで{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I peel off the skin and eat it.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{壁紙|かべがみ}を{剥|は}いでから{新|あたら}しいのを{貼|は}った。
examples.english: I put up new wallpaper after stripping off the old one.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}は{被害者|ひがいしゃ}の{服|ふく}を{剥|は}いで{逃|に}げた。
examples.english: The thief stripped the victim of their clothes and fled.

notes:
Conjugates as a godan verb: {剥|は}がない, {剥|は}いで, {剥|は}いだ. The action is more forceful and rough compared to {剥|む}く (to peel gently, as with fruit).

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{剥|は}ぐ — to strip/tear off (forceful removal of a covering)
・{剥|む}く — to peel (gentler; fruit, vegetables)
・{剥|は}がす — to peel off, to remove (stickers, labels, tape)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{皮|かわ}を{剥|は}ぐ (to strip off skin/bark)
・{服|ふく}を{剥|は}ぐ (to strip someone of clothes)
・{仮面|かめん}を{剥|は}ぐ (to tear off a mask — also figurative)
